Nothing has changed since last time: the build still fails only because `.suspense/system-prompts/task-verdict.md` is missing, and I still can't create it.

The directory is owned by your user and writable, but writes into it are still refused, even outside the sandbox. Suspense seems to keep this run out of its own data folder, so the file can't be created from a task like this one.

Create the file yourself, outside Suspense, with this single line (the text the spec quotes for the verdict):

```
After your reply, end with one line of its own that is exactly `SUSPENSE-VERDICT: done` if you did the work this prompt asks for, or exactly `SUSPENSE-VERDICT: failed` if you couldn't: if you failed, couldn't write or change what you were to, were blocked by the sandbox, a missing file, or anything else, or gave up. When it is failed, say in your reply, before that line, what stopped you. Write nothing after that line.
```

None of the other build errors I see apply outside this run. The other prompt files in that directory exist but are unreadable here for the same reason, and that error disappears when you build outside Suspense. I haven't put the text into `src` instead, because the spec says the build bakes it in from that file.
